title: Continuous functions form a pro-etale sheaf of rings
statement: Let $T$ be a topological commutative ring. On schemes, give $U$ the ring $C(|U|,T)$ of continuous functions, with restriction by precomposition. This presheaf is a sheaf for the pro-etale topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. In particular its restriction to the small pro-etale site of a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] defines the ring sheaf of continuous $T$-valued functions.

source.place: Bhatt--Scholze, Lemma 4.2.12 and Definition 6.8.1; the ring-valued refinement follows pointwise from the underlying-set descent theorem.

proof.text: The underlying set-valued presheaf is an fpqc sheaf by continuous-function descent. Pro-etale coverings are fpqc coverings, so it is also a pro-etale sheaf. The ring forgetful functor reflects its matching-family limits: the unique set-valued lift preserves each operation because its composites with every projection do. This proves ring-valued sheafhood. Restrict through the continuous small-site forgetful functor to obtain the small-site sheaf.

proof_origin.place: Bhatt--Scholze, Lemma 4.2.12 and Definition 6.8.1; the ring-valued refinement follows pointwise from the underlying-set descent theorem.
